title: Shortest common superstrings
author: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)
description: OpenAI's deterministic polynomial-time algorithm (2026) that finds, for every finite family of strings, a common superstring at most twice as long as the shortest one. The first lesson sets up the hierarchical graph of substrings, in which closed walks through the empty word spell superstrings, and Euler tours. The second constructs forced occurrence counts, including a rule for periodic words, and a balanced base graph of cost W <= OPT. The third rearranges the base graph into periodic layers with budgets adding up to W and proves two facts about periodic texts. The fourth connects all layers to the empty word at extra cost at most W.
